title: iOS 27.3 Beta Adds Daily Siri AI Limits and iCloud+ Upgrades
content:
With the latest iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 betas, Apple is starting to test limits and paid upgrades for Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features.
Every Apple device gets a free daily access allowance for Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features that rely on server-side AI processing, such as Image Playground and Clean Up in Photos. When that limit is hit, there will be an option to extend usage with an iCloud+ plan. Here's what will be limited after the daily allowance has been reached:
- Siri AI for multi-step, personal context requests that rely on server-side processing, such as asking Siri what time you need to leave from home to make it to a location on time.
- Image generation and editing tools, including Image Playground and the AI options in Photos like Clean Up, Extend, and Spatial Reframing.
- Workflows and automations in Shortcuts that rely on AFM Cloud and AFM Cloud Pro.
- Third-party apps that use Apple Foundation Models in Private Cloud Compute for AI features.
While more complex, multi-step requests will be restricted, basic Siri commands will continue to be available even after a device limit is reached. Examples of basic Siri commands include those with a single ask, such as "set a timer for 30 minutes" or "text Eric I'm on my way."
Apple's existing iCloud+ plans will include higher daily usage for Siri AI and Apple Intelligence, with no change in pricing. If you already subscribe to an eligible iCloud+ plan, you will have higher usage limits. Free limits are per device, not per account, and do not roll over.
More access starts with the 200GB iCloud+ plan, which is priced at $2.99 per month. Users who subscribe to this plan have up to a 2x usage limit. Users who subscribe to the $9.99/month 2TB plan get up to 5x usage. The $29.99/month 6TB plan comes with up to 10x usage, and the $59.99/month 12TB plan offers up to 20x usage. Family members who share a plan will have a shared usage pool.
- 50GB - No limit increase
- 200GB - Up to 2x limit
- 2TB - Up to 5x limit
- 6TB - Up to 10x limit
- 12TB - Up to 20x limit
Every Apple device will use the free daily limit first, and when that's reached, Siri AI and Apple Intelligence will use the iCloud+ paid access. In a family group, a device that hits the free limit will start drawing from the shared pool on a first-come, first-served basis. Limits will reset at around 12:00 a.m. in the user's current time zone, and in families, the reset is based on the plan purchaser's time zone.
Each of the four categories has a different limit, and Apple will likely use the beta testing period to refine those limits and make sure people aren't hitting their caps too quickly. Limits depend on feature category, request complexity, and system demand, and they could change over time.
Apple plans to give warnings when people are approaching their limits, and a notification when the limit has been hit. From there, users will be able to purchase additional access through an iCloud+ plan, or wait for their limit to reset.
Apple is not planning to offer additional usage beyond what's available with the 12TB iCloud+ plan at this time.

report.summary: Apple's iOS 27.3 beta introduces free daily caps on server-side Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features, with paid iCloud+ tiers unlocking 2x to 20x more usage.
report.background: Apple introduced Apple Intelligence in 2024 as a free feature set, mixing on-device models with Private Cloud Compute servers for heavier tasks. Running large-model inference at scale is expensive, and Apple has been under pressure to show services revenue growth as hardware sales mature. iCloud+ — a storage subscription with a huge installed base — is the natural billing rail, since Apple can raise AI quotas without changing the sticker price. The move mirrors a broader industry shift: OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic all meter or tier their most capable models, and 'unlimited AI' bundles are disappearing. Apple's pitch is that privacy-preserving server AI still needs a funding model, and that most people's daily usage is light enough to stay inside the free allowance.
key_points: Every device gets a free daily allowance for server-side Apple Intelligence work. When it runs out, complex requests are blocked until roughly midnight local time; allowances do not roll over and are counted per device, not per Apple Account. Simple one-shot Siri commands — timers, messages, alarms — keep working regardless.

Four categories are metered: multi-step Siri requests that use personal context, image generation and editing (Image Playground, Clean Up, Extend, Spatial Reframing), Shortcuts automations running on AFM Cloud or AFM Cloud Pro, and third-party apps calling Apple Foundation Models in Private Cloud Compute. Each category has its own cap, adjusted for request complexity and system demand.

Paid relief comes through existing iCloud+ tiers at unchanged prices: 200GB ($2.99) doubles limits, 2TB ($9.99) gives 5x, 6TB ($29.99) 10x, 12TB ($59.99) 20x. The 50GB plan gets nothing extra. Family plans share one pool, consumed first-come, first-served, with resets tied to the plan purchaser's time zone.

Apple will warn users as they approach a cap and notify them when it is hit, offering an upgrade path or a wait. Because limits depend on category, complexity, and server load, the numbers in this beta are explicitly provisional — Apple says it will use the testing period to tune them so people are not hitting walls too quickly.

There is a hard ceiling: Apple says it will not sell usage beyond the 12TB plan's 20x allowance for now. That caps how much heavy AI work — say, automated image pipelines or agentic Shortcuts — any single subscriber can run, and leaves room for Apple to introduce higher tiers or a dedicated AI subscription later.
report.impact: For Apple, this is the first real price tag on Apple Intelligence: AI becomes a services revenue line rather than a free differentiator, and iCloud+ upgrades become an AI upsell. Developers building on Apple Foundation Models inherit a quota their users can exhaust, so apps need graceful fallbacks, on-device alternatives, and clear messaging — or they will absorb blame for Apple's limits. Regular users get a familiar 'free tier plus subscription' model, but also a new anxiety: watching a daily AI meter. If the free allowance feels stingy, expect backlash and pressure on Apple to raise it; if it is generous, the caps mostly push heavy users and families toward bigger storage plans. Either way, 'unlimited AI' just became a thing of the past on Apple platforms.
report.tools: Follow Apple's Foundation Models framework documentation and the Private Cloud Compute security blog to see how quotas are enforced and what on-device fallbacks exist. Test your own usage in the beta via Settings > Apple Intelligence and the Feedback Assistant. For local, unmetered alternatives, try Ollama or LM Studio for LLM inference, and ComfyUI or Draw Things for image generation on Apple silicon. Shortcuts users should audit AFM Cloud automations and move routine work to on-device actions.
